articleTitle: Wide-Angle and Polarization Insensitive Dual-Band Metamaterial Absorber
abstract: This paper presents a single layer wide-angle and polarization insensitive compact metamaterial absorber for dual- band (C- and X- bands) operation. The unit cell of the proposed absorber is made up of two modified concentric circular rings printed on a grounded dielectric substrate. The surface power loss distribution on the unit cell confirms the dual-band nature. A planar absorber fabricated with 25x25 unit cells is tested for its absorption characteristics and found to exhibit more than 99% absorptivity at both 5.2 GHz and 10.4 GHz frequency bands. The proposed dual-band absorber maintains its absorptivity for various polarization angles and wide-angles of incidence.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of Conducted Emission For Electronic Control Module
abstract: This paper deals with modelling and simulation of Conducted emission of an Electronic Control Unit (ECU) which carries multiple switching elements like switch mode power supply and output drivers. The simulation model includes LISN model, behavior of discrete components in the form of SPICE model and the parasitics of PCB. At PCB the SMPS power supply buck topology with 2 MHz switching frequency and H Bridge driver with 2 KHz switching frequency is used. The peak spectral plot from simulation is used to evaluate the design and identify the noise source in design. Simulation and measurement results are compared to know area of improvement in simulation modelling approach. This paper also highlights effect of adding parasitics into simulation.

articleTitle: Electrical Impedance Tomography - Differential Solutions
abstract: Topological derivative application to electrically conducting material having various characteristics, its implication on how this influences the result of obtaining an image with increased intensity on regions of organs with appreciable results compared to existing techniques is the main theme of this paper. Characteristic function, Lebesgue space, weak derivative and distributional derivative helps to get an enhanced image with ne plus ultra results. Introducing inclusions in the conducting region and arriving at shape derived results for the domain forms part of the problem. Image processing techniques and Shape derivative problem go hand in hand. Finally application of Hessian matrix and the Strum Liouville operator to regions brought in focus by the impedance tomography helps to obtain results in pinpointed way is brought out.

articleTitle: Hybrid Complementary FSS Element based on Fibonacci Spiral for Triple-band EMI Shielding Application
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) caused by microwave sources leads to the malfunction and faulty readings of many real-time systems. Hence it is essential to provide EMI shielding for sensitive electronic devises anwd chambers. An array of periodic elements offers advantages such as transparency and opacity at selected frequencies with lower weight. In this regard, a complementary frequency selective surfaces (CFSS) has been analyzed for EMI shielding application. The CFSS exhibits a highly stable response with three controllable passbands for normal and oblique incidences. Such response is more suitable for allowing selective frequency bands with strong stopband between them.

articleTitle: Low Cost Conducted EMI Measurement on Site for Product EMC Pre-compliance
abstract: This paper proposes a low cost product conducted EMI measurement solution. The solution employs a general oscilloscope plus Cloud Computing to make conducted EMI measurement on manufacture's workshop, to save time and expense of sending products through multiple rounds of compliance measurement at the test house. An EMI-separation-device based on enhanced EMI filter is introduced and grounding contribution to conducted EMI measurement is studied to ensure success of measurement on site. An application example is given showing the conducted EMI measurement on site through oscilloscope plus Cloud Computing is fast and low cost.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Ground Field Sensor for EMP Measurement
abstract: Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) is a high amplitude, short duration, broadband pulse of electromagnetic energy which can have destructive effects on susceptible electronic types of equipment and systems. In this paper Model & Simulation analysis of ground field derivative sensor carried out for measurement of short duration EMP pulses. For generating EMP pulse, open TEM cell has been modeled and characterized in terms of return loss (S11) and VSWR. EMP field uniformly between TEM plates has obtained. Ground field sensor modeled and mounted on the bottom plate of the TEM cell. Simulation analysis of modeled ground field sensor for measurement of fast EMP pulse carried out. Simulation results are compared with practical results measured using commercially available field sensors. Simulation and measurement results are in close agreement.

articleTitle: Estimating Far-Field EMI from CM current of Buck Converter
abstract: Switch mode power supplies (SMPS) are widely used for their high efficiency, low weight and volume. But they generate Electromagnetic Interference due to high switching frequency. They generate EMI in conducted and radiated frequencies which may be above the accepted international standards. The Radiated Emission affects the performance of the nearby sensitive electronic integrated circuits. As per the international standards the radiated emission frequency ranges from 30MHz to 3GHz. Hence this range of frequencies is investigated here. In this paper a method to estimate the radiated EMI due to Common Mode currents flowing in SMPS is presented. In a buck converter, the CM currents due to different prominent coupling capacitors are calculated. The configuration giving the highest CM current is considered. The far field Radiated emission due to this current at 1m and 3m distance is calculated and is presented.

articleTitle: Conductor Backed Coplanar Waveguide Bandpass Filter using Vertically Loaded Coupled Open-ended Stubs
abstract: In this paper, a Conductor backed coplanar waveguide (CB-CPW) 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order bandpass filter is designed using Coupled open ended stub resonator placed vertically to the signal line. Vertically loaded open ended stubs are designed at quarter wavelength so as to behave like a short circuit at the input terminal thus giving a band-accepted response with lesser metallic area or minimum size. Four such coupled open ended resonators are placed in series and also in closely manner to provide greater field confinement of the proposed bandpass filter. The bandpass filter is designed for a centre frequency of 2.5 GHz with FBW of 97.89%, insertion loss of <; 0.5dB, rising and falling edge selectivity of 30.75 dB/GHz and 27.01dB/GHz respectively with a wide stopband of around 4GHz after the desired passband.

articleTitle: Effect of Penetrating Conductors on Enclosure HEMP Hardening
abstract: An electromagnetic modelling and simulation analysis carried out to study the effect of penetrating conductors on EMP Shielding Effectiveness (SE) of the shielded enclosure. Transient electromagnetic fields from an EMP source, which can induce currents into a conductor. This current will continue to flow on the conductor as it penetrates the shield boundary. The current flowing in the conductor will cause the re-radiation of an EMP field on the other side of the shielding boundary. For both plane wave and transient EMP SE with different positions of cable penetration into the shielded enclosure was analyzed, and based on the obtained results it recommends suitable cable penetration, to minimize the fields coupling inside the enclosure. This investigation will be utilized for routing the cables from the external electromagnetic environment to protect sensitive electronics systems inside the enclosure.

articleTitle: Coupling Analysis of EMP and UWB Fast Transients on PCB Traces
abstract: With the Exponential increase in use of electronics, Intentional Electromagnetic interference (IEMI) pose a greater threat not only for Military Sector, civilian sector as well. There is a potential threat from Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) attack on Telecom, Radar, Electric Power, Banking and Financial service etc. High Power microwave energy illuminated over vital installation can jam electronic equipment information. In the present study, Structures radiating two different fast transients pulses Viz, EMP and Ultra-Wide Band (UWB) system with different pulse characteristics viz., rise time and frequency content were modeled using 3D EM simulation tool CST. Coupling effects of two different fast transients pulse from IEMI sources EMP, UWB on PCB Traces were studied and presented.

articleTitle: HEMP Hardening of Shielded Enclosure for Critical Equipment Protection
abstract: Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) is transient pulse of electromagnetic field which can interference the electrical & electronic systems. The wireless communication, defence, industry and now extended to Consumer sectors are major victims for the electromagnetic pulse. The Shielded Enclosure offers shielding against the intentional & un-intentional electromagnetic radiations. Shielding of EM waves can be done through the reflection, absorption, multiple reflections by the shield/ barrier. The metals and their alloys can be used as the shields.In this paper, it is proposed to develop rectangular enclosure for providing hardening against HEMP. 3D EM Modeling and simulation analysis carried out by modeling the bounded wave EMP antenna and rectangular enclosure. HEMP hardening obtained in simulations compared with practical measurements carried out using D-dot sensor.

articleTitle: Performance Validation of ALSE Using In-house Fabricated Long Wire Antenna
abstract: The International standard CISPR 25 is applicable to any electrical/electronic component intended for use in vehicles, trailers and devices. In order to minimize the effect of Absorber Lined Shielded Enclosure (ALSE) on measured electric field, the latest edition of CISPR 25 has introduced a procedure in Annexure J for validation of ALSEs in the frequency range of 150 kHz to 1 GHz. The standard proposed two methods for ALSE validation viz. Reference measurement method and Modelled long wire antenna method. In this paper, validation of SAMEER's Semi-Anechoic Chamber (SAC) using Modelled long wire antenna method is explained. Design and fabrication details of long wire antenna along with measured results are also presented.

articleTitle: Field Homogeneity and Quite Zone of India’s Largest EMP Facility
abstract: Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) is a short burst of electromagnetic energy which can disrupt the electrical and electronic systems. This paper mainly focuses on Field Homogeneity and quite zone areas identification of India’s Largest Outdoor RS105, EMP Test Facility. Modeling & Simulation analysis of bounded wave EMP antenna was carried out to verify the field uniformity as per the standard. Simulated results are verified with practical results after commissioning the EMP facility to meet the compliance testing for RS105 as per the MIL standards with generated test levels more than 50 kV/m and covering the EUT test volume of 17m(L)X12m(W)X3m(H), sufficient to test the large defence and civilian systems.Quite Zone area has been marked as per ICNIRP guidelines after simulation and practical field survey measurements carried out around the facility.

articleTitle: Characterization of Derivative Sensor Without Using Transient Source
abstract: Derivative sensors (D dot and B dot) are used for measurement of transient electric and magnetic fields mainly from Electromagnetic pulse (EMP) and lightning events. These sensors are characterized by using standard field generation method like monocone antenna and TEM cell methods. This paper discusses the methodology for characterizing the sensors from its frequency domain transfer function, which in turn can be used for measuring the transient signals.

articleTitle: ESD (Electrostaic Discharge) Soft Failure Risk Assessment For a Thin Display Metal Back Cover
abstract: Most of the connected electronic devices such as smart phone, tablet and laptop has LCD (liquid crystal display) with metal back plate as a part of system stack up. The metal back plate of the display helps in grounding the system ingredients and FPC (Flexible Printed Circuits) into the chassis/ system ground which helps to prevent the ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) soft failures and its thickness is around 0.5mm. But as the devices are trending towards more and more thin designs the thickness of the display metal back cover becomes a problem. The paper provides an ESD soft failure risk assessment where the thick display metal back cover is replaced with a less than 0.05mm thin metal sheet and its effect on ESD soft failure is studied. The paper covers following key topics: a) creation of an ESD pass and fail case for a given issue, b) identification of correct measurement parameters in simulation to distinguish between pass and fail case, c) validation of an ESD simulation setup with the help of Z parameter correlation and d) assessment of ESD soft failure using a thick display metal back cover and using a thin metal sheet. The ESD soft failure risk assessment is performed using 3D EM simulation and identified surface current on the system ground as a critical part of soft failure mechanism.
